body.p: This paper is filed in response to the Office Action mailed August 27, 2024 (hereinafter "Office Action") in connection with the above-referenced application. By way of summary, claims 1-19 were pending in this application. In this paper, Applicant has canceled claims without prejudice or disclaimer, amended claims without prejudice or disclaimer to their previously presented versions, and added a claim. No new matter is added. Applicant reserves the right to pursue the previously pending claims and/or subject matter of the previously pending claims in this or another application. Accordingly, claims 1-2, 4-5, and 8-20 are pending for consideration.
Discussion of Claim Re jections - 35 US.C. ? 102

Claims 1-7, 9-11, and 16-19 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. @ 102(a)(1) as being allegedly anticipated by U.S. Publication No. 2019/0090766 to Block et al. ("Block"). Applicant respectfully traverses each rejection, each finding of fact, including each assertion regarding what the references show or teach, and any rationales for modifying or combining the references, and Applicant does not acquiesce in the validity of the rejections. To expedite allowance of this application, however, Applicant has amended the claims as set forth herein.
Amended independent claim 1 recites the following (emphasis added for discussion purposes only):
An optical physiological sensor integrated into a wearable device, the optical physiological sensor comprising: a substrate having an optical center;
a first emitter group of light emitting diodes (LEDs) positioned adjacent to the optical center of the substrate and spaced at an offset from
the optical center;

a second emitter group of LEDs positioned adjacent to the optical center of the substrate at an offset to the optical center and spaced at an offset from the optical center opposite the first emitter group of LEDs
relative to the optical center; and

a plurality of detectors arranged in a spatial configuration that surrounds the first and the second emitter group, wherein each of the plurality of detectors are positioned on the substrate a same distance away
from the optical center of the substrate; and

a light barrier construct mounted on the substrate and defining a first emitter chamber that houses the first emitter group of LEDs, and a second emitter chamber that houses the second emitter group of LEDs, wherein the light barrier construct is configured to optically isolate the
first emitter group of LEDs from the second emitter group of LEDs.

For at least the reasons discussed during the interview on October 2, 2024 and because Block fails to expressly or inherently disclose at least the above-emphasized features of amended independent claim 1, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 is not anticipated by Block.

FIGS. 27A and 27E of the present application (reproduced below) illustrate a nonlimiting implementation of the sensor recited in claim 1. As shown, a first emitter chamber 2736a houses a first emitter group of LEDS and a second emitter chamber 2736b houses a second emitter group of LEDS. The first and second emitter chambers are separated by a light barrier construct 2720. Accordingly, the light barrier construct as recited in claim 1 isolates entire groups of LEDS. FIGS. 27A and 27E also show detectors 2706 surrounding both the first and second emitter groups such that each detector 2706 is equal distance away from the center C1.
Claim 8 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being allegedly unpatentable over Block as applied to claim 1, and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 11,857,298 to Allee ("Allee").
Claims 12-15 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being allegedly unpatentable over Block as applied to claim 1, and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 10,987,054 to Pandya ("Pandya").

Applicant respectfully traverses each rejection, each finding of fact, including each assertion regarding what the references show or teach, and any rationales for modifying or combining the references, and Applicant does not acquiesce in the validity of the rejections. To
expedite allowance of this application, however, Applicant has amended the claims as set forth herein. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of each rejection.

Dependent claims 8 and 12-15 are also allowable over the cited references at least because the features discussed above with regard to the § 102 rejection with respect to claim 1 are not taught or suggested by the art cited in the rejection of the claims as obvious and also because each of these dependent claims recites a unique combination of features not taught or suggested by the cited references, alone or in combination. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103.

Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are not patentable. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application. Applicant reserves the right to pursue at a later date any previously pending or other broader or narrower claims that capture any subject matter supported by the present disclosure, including subject matter found to be specifically disclaimed herein or by any prior prosecution. Accordingly, reviewers of this or any parent, child or related prosecution history shall not reasonably infer that Applicant has made any disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the present application.
Please charge any additional fees, including any fees for additional extension of time, or credit overpayment to Deposit Account No. 11-1410.
Respectfully submitted,
